subject: Headroom safety slab proposal and discount reconciliation
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@launchlane.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Headroom safety slab proposal and next steps

Hi Samir,

Congrats again on LaunchLane's pilot going into week two — traffic looks great and the model latency has been steady. We spotted an unexpected shortfall vs the committed throughput in your PO window last night that pushed you above the soft quota for ~18 hours.

Before formal invoicing, I wanted to propose a pragmatic path so you can keep the launch momentum without billing surprises:

- Short-term: offer a 14-day headroom safety slab (temporary buffer) that covers the observed overrun while we stitch in autoscale guardrails.
- Pricing: slab priced at a blended 30% of our normal overrun rate (proportional to the overrun tokens), capped at the equivalent of one week of peak usage.
- True-up: we will reconcile actual usage at the end of the 14-day window and apply a one-time proration credit if you switch to a committed tier.

I've attached a short proposal (headroom_safety_slab_proposal.pdf) and the Q1 usage export for your finance team. If this sounds reasonable I can loop in Ben from pricing to get a formal amendment ready and pass to procurement.

Quick ask: can the procurement email (procure@launchlane.com) confirm whether a PO amendment or a short-term addendum is easier on your side?

Thanks,
Jonas

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: headroom_safety_slab_proposal.pdf)
From: Samir Patel <samir@launchlane.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Headroom safety slab proposal and next steps

Jonas — thank you, appreciate the proactive reach.

We saw the same spike overnight. This was caused by an integration bug in our routing mesh that sent a high retry rate to the inference endpoint. We have a fix staged but it will take a few hours to fully roll out.

Procurement prefers an addendum over reissuing the PO for speed. Two asks from our side:

1) Can you confirm the exact token bucket you used to calculate the 30% blended slab (so we can validate with our numbers)?
2) Would you consider a one-time 10% discount on the slab if we commit to a 6-month reserved capacity bump immediately (we're willing to discuss tiers)?

I'll cc procurement (procure@launchlane.com) now. I can get internal sign-off quickly if we have numbers and a document they can countersign.

— Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, LaunchLane
(Attachment: none)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@launchlane.com>, procure@launchlane.com
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Headroom safety slab proposal and next steps — pricing clarification requested

Ben / Laura,

Looping you in — LaunchLane asked for the slab calculation and is requesting a conditional 10% one-time discount if they commit to a 6-month reserved bump. Quick context:

- Observable overrun: ~1.8x their average hourly qps for a ~18 hour window. See usage_report_Q1.csv attached.
- Proposed slab pricing: 30% of standard overrun rate, capped. It is meant to be a temporary safety buffer not a permanent discount.

Samir is open to immediate committed capacity which could be valuable ARR. If we can provide a clear calculation (tokens and dollar estimate) and a small introductory concession, I think we can lock the commit. Can we run numbers for a one-time 10% off the slab (conditional on a 6-month commit at X capacity) and produce an amendment draft they can sign today?

Ben — can you model the impact quickly? Laura — will legal need special language for a short-term addendum vs PO amendment?

Thanks,
Jonas
(Attachment: usage_report_Q1.csv)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@launchlane.com>, procure@launchlane.com
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2026 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Headroom safety slab proposal and next steps — pricing clarification requested

Quick reply with numbers so we can get Samir into procurement:

- Calculation basis: overrun tokens = sum of generated + prompt tokens during the 18-hour window above their contracted QPS baseline (baseline = average of prior 30 days). Using their export, that's ~47.2M tokens.
- Standard overrun rate: $0.0009 per token (their current pay-as-you-go).
- Proposed slab charge at 30%: 47.2M * $0.0009 * 0.30 = $12,744 (pre-cap).
- Cap: we set a slab cap equal to one week of their historical peak spend (~$25k) so this stays bounded.
- If we apply a one-time 10% concession on the slab: $12,744 * 0.90 = $11,469.60.

Commercial ask: in exchange for the 10% concession, require a 6-month reserved commitment for an additional 25% concurrency (specific tier: Dedicated 3 slot bump), with a 30-day notice clause for downgrade at term end. That commitment should be included in the amendment.

Laura — I recommend the addendum flow (short signature page + fee table) rather than reissuing the PO; faster and less procurement friction. I'll attach a draft amendment and the token calc in the doc Ben will build and share.

Samir / procurement — if that tradeoff looks workable I'll get the amendment over for signature and we can mark the temporary slab applied immediately (invoice deferred until amendment executed).

Ben Carter
Senior Pricing Analyst
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: amendment_draft.docx)
